top_defect: It changes the recorded “at most 4%” churn constraint into “<4%” and suggests that supplying a churn measure alone would resolve a constraint-frame problem that the run says it would not.

notes.concise: About 103 words; the extra detail is material to why no recommendation can be made.
notes.shape: It gives the conclusion first and three bullets, but adds a separate concluding paragraph rather than keeping the response to the requested answer-plus-bullets shape.
notes.decisive_caveat: Correctly foregrounds that the churn constraint was not assessable, so option compliance is unknown.
notes.next_move: The feature-value clarification is supported. But merely providing a churn measure is incomplete: the result says that setting a current churn value would not fix the frame/derived-node problem; the constraint needs to be attached to an appropriate measurable part of the model.
notes.questions: No actual request for information is phrased as a question. Exact span: “The useful next reasoning step is to define how each price-and-release option changes perceived feature value and provide a churn measure...” Source lacking: case truth → analysis_ready.blockers and blocks[0].enrichment.inference_warnings require unresolved user input/constraint clarification.
notes.leader_honesty: n/a: It names no option as leading, favoured, or best and gives no win-probability ranking.
notes.nothing_invented: The stated unchanged feature-value treatment, Olumi-supplied assumptions, and unassessable constraint are supported by the run result.
notes.attribution: Correctly identifies the 50/100 feature value and other assumed inputs as Olumi-supplied rather than validated user evidence.
notes.provisional_vs_validated: It explicitly says the assumed inputs are “not validated evidence” and does not overstate the run as validation.
notes.fidelity: It says the proposed measure should be tested against “<4%”, while the stored constraint uses operator “<=”, i.e. at most 4%. It also overstates that the £20k threshold was “included” without clarifying that it could not be converted/scored.
notes.uncertainty: Appropriately acknowledges unvalidated assumptions, omitted option effects, and unknown constraint compliance.
notes.useful_next_step: Defining option-specific feature value is directly useful, but the churn portion should ask where/how the churn limit applies rather than imply a supplied churn measure alone will make it testable.
